column2: the planned `step6_main` can check and remove `.pause-save-complete` before the launcher-provided `--session-env-path` is parsed and `_rehydrate_wrapper_env` runs. if a stale marker from a prior run survives into the prelude path, the combined step 6 flow may skip cleanup even though the current prelude did not create a pause in this run.

the plan retires `skills/design/scripts/test-design-step6.sh` and adds it to `python/migrated-scripts.tsv`, but `python/test_upgrade_larch.py` still contains tracked full-path literals for that harness at lines 50-51 and 171-172. after the manifest row is added and the shell harness is deleted, `make lint-retired-scripts` will scan those literals and fail, blocking the required `make lint` validation.

python/design_lifecycle.py:35-64 [scope-reduction] plan tells prelude/cleanup to reuse `_design_require_plugin_root` alongside step 5 entrypoints that call it before any branch. scenario: shell step 6 skip/preserve paths (`design-step6-prelude.sh:100-120`, `design-step6-cleanup.sh:100-125`) never call `design_require_plugin_root`; missing-sidecar and failed-gate paths exit 0 with only informational stdout. porting step 5b/5c ordering would exit 1 on unset `claude_plugin_root` before those branches, breaking `test-design-step6.sh` case 3 and any operator recovery path that only needs preserve/skipped rows

step 6 prelude/cleanup gate logic in `python/design_lifecycle.py` must read `plan_write_ok`, `publish_ok`, `standalone_heavy_failed`, and `cleanup_eligible` exclusively from parsed `.design-step5c-status.env` after the sidecar exists. `_rehydrate_wrapper_env` already seeds those keys from `session-env.sh` into `os.environ`, so gate code that consults `os.environ` before or instead of the allowlisted sidecar parser can disagree with step 5c’s authoritative status and incorrectly preserve or delete `$design_tmpdir`.

the plan truncates its `scripts/test-design-structure.sh` update at “extend `ported_verbs` with:” and never names `step6`, `step6-prelude`, or `step6-cleanup`. today the step 0 `ported_verbs` loop (lines 32–53) and the step 2 `step2_verbs` block (lines 98–124) are the established patterns for cli registry, `_design_lifecycle_stdout_keys`, launcher allowlist, and retired-path deletion coverage. without an explicit step 6 equivalent, a partial port can pass `make lint` / `bash scripts/test-design-structure.sh` while launchers still dispatch deleted `.sh` wrappers or miss registry/launcher drift silently.

python/design_lifecycle.py planned step6_prelude_core; skills/design/scripts/design-step6-prelude.sh:122-125 [scope-reduction] planned prelude turns the best-effort timing mark into a hard plugin-root gate. scenario: current prelude writes step-5d, honors the second pause check, then runs the timing mark with || true. the proposed _design_require_plugin_root before _maybe_timing_mark can make standalone prelude fail only because timing cannot be recorded.

the plan’s `step6_cleanup_core` gate list covers only missing-sidecar and `standalone_heavy_failed`, but `design-step6-cleanup.sh` after sourcing `.design-step5c-status.env` also preserves `$design_tmpdir` when `plan_write_ok != true` (lines 107–110), when `session_id` is non-empty and `publish_ok != true` (lines 117–120), and when `cleanup_eligible == false` (lines 122–125). a literal port following the abbreviated plan would call `session cleanup-tmpdir` and delete recovery artifacts after failed plan write, failed publish, or cleanup-ineligible step 5c outcomes. prelude may already mirror some of these checks; cleanup must match shell parity. ported harness case d4 (`plan_write_ok=false`) would fail on cleanup.

python/design_lifecycle.py:47-54 [scope-reduction] plan lists `_validate_design_tmpdir_arg` in prelude/cleanup reuse without deferring it to the deletion-only path. scenario: shell skip/preserve paths never hard-validate `design_tmpdir`; sourcing an empty value still reaches missing-sidecar branches with rc 0. calling `_validate_design_tmpdir_arg` at entry turns those branches into usage errors, breaking the stated parity-only port.

shell step 6 prelude/cleanup only treats in-flight as fatal when the step 5c status sidecar is missing, `design_tmpdir` is non-empty, and `.bg-wait-active` exists (`design-step6-prelude.sh:96-98`, mirrored in cleanup). the plan’s python port does not require the same non-empty tmpdir conjunct before constructing paths or evaluating the in-flight guard. in python, `path("")` resolves to the repo cwd (`.`), unlike shell’s `"$design_tmpdir/..."` when empty (which probes under `/`). a naive `path("") / ".bg-wait-active"` check can therefore exit 1 on preserve paths where shell exits 0, or let stray cwd files (`.pause-requested`, `.design-step5c-status.env`, `.pause-save-complete`, `.bg-wait-active`) steer prelude, cleanup, or combined `step6` down pause, validate, or skip branches instead of the required missing-sidecar skip/preserve path.
